subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` calls fail closed for existing ownerless session rows, even though upgraded plugin workflows may lose patch access to those rows?
rationale: No plugin identity can be safely inferred for an ownerless row; allowing first-writer adoption would reopen the cross-plugin authority problem, while rejection creates an intentional compatibility boundary that requires repository owner acceptance.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, retain operator/non-plugin recovery, and document the upgrade behavior in the PR evidence.

options.title: Add an explicit migration owner
options.body: Define a trusted doctor or operator migration that assigns ownership only from authoritative provenance before plugin-runtime patching is allowed.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Allow plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, accepting that the first plugin to patch can effectively claim or mutate legacy state.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, retain operator/non-plugin recovery, and document the upgrade behavior in the PR evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the adjacent session lifecycle/delete contract and the central gateway handler where the compatibility decision lands.
